title: Limits and harms in history texts
statement: In history texts, show an achievement's limits and never play down the harm done to the people it affected.
detail: Notes on a curriculum map's history texts ask that a text on the birth of democracy discuss its limitations, and that a text on the first peoples of the Americas, and those after it, not downplay the tragedy of European arrival (`downloads/_G3 curriculum Map.xlsx - Curric Map.csv`). The map's source record for a folk tale from an oral tradition asks for a respectful retelling (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Curriculum maps/_G3 curriculum Map.xlsx`). These are notes on particular texts, so the rule covers only the kinds of text they concern. A second learning sits in the same notes: retell other peoples' traditional stories with respect.

evidence.quote: Ensure the limitations of Ancient Greek democracy are discussed.
Be really careful here to not downplay the tragedy of European arrival for those already in the Americas (ditto with texts below).
A single triumphant account would be historically and pedagogically defective
Do not use "democracy expanded" without naming for whom; do not present reform as one unified movement or the Market Revolution as an automatic, single-cause transformation.
Do not equate industrial growth with shared prosperity, treat the West as empty land, or describe government as simply absent from the economy.
The feedback gate rejects claims that turn unequal consequences into a neutral swap.
